Indian benchmark indices witnessed profit booking on October 14 as rising crude oil prices and persistent foreign investor outflows weighed on sentiment.
At close, the Sensex was down 251.89 points or 0.34 percent at 72,781.89, and the Nifty was down 99.25 points or 0.44 percent at 22,622.70.
Among broader indices, the Nifty midcap and smallcap indices ended with marginal losses.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Flat)
GIFT Nifty was trading flat at around 22,625 in early trade, indicating a flat opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Markets (Slip)

Markets started the day on the back foot as trading kicked off in Asia on Thursday, as a quicker-than-expected increase in US consumer price inflation upped expectations for the Federal Reserve to act later this year and pushed stocks lower.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 1.2%, led by a 7% plunge in South Korea's KOSPI, while the Nikkei 225 fell 3.8%. S&P 500 e-mini futures were down 0.3%.
US Equities (Down)

Hotter-than-expected inflation data sent the Nasdaq ​to a sharply lower close on Wednesday, with worries about more interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve pummeling ‌shares of Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sensitive to higher borrowing costs.
The S&P 500 declined 1.11% to end the session at 7,718.94 points, its biggest one-day drop since July 29.
The Nasdaq declined 1.88% to ​26,692.87 points, its biggest daily drop since July 23. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.09% to 51,621.48 points.
Dollar Index (Slips)
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, trading at 102.1.
US Bond Yield (Down)
The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond fell 5.8 basis points to 5.12%, and yield on the US 2-year Treasury bond fell 6.7 basis points to 4.72%.
Asian Currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar in early trade, with the South Korean won emerging as the biggest loser, declining 0.77 percent from its previous close. The Taiwan dollar also weakened by 0.24 percent, while the Chinese renminbi slipped 0.06 percent. The Indonesian rupiah, Philippine peso and Malaysian ringgit edged lower by 0.02 percent, 0.01 percent and 0.005 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Japanese yen appreciated 0.43 percent, posting the strongest gain among its regional peers, followed by the Singapore dollar, which rose 0.23 percent. The Thai baht also strengthened by 0.24 percent against the US dollar.
Crude (Down)
Oil held a gain as a flare-up in attacks from Russia to the Middle East threatened supply that only recently recovered to near pre-Iran War levels.
Brent traded around $106 a barrel after rising 1.3% in the week’s first three sessions, while West Texas Intermediate was below $95.
Gold (Up)
Gold held a decline as a jump in US inflation stoked worries the Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates further to keep prices under control.
Bullion traded near $4,105 an ounce after slumping 1.3% the day before, while silver held a 6% loss from the previous session.
Fund Flow Action
On October 14, Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth around Rs 1,857 crore, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought equities of Rs 2,670 crore during the session.
